items.title: Stubborn Belly Fat Starts In Your Liver (Here's The Fix)
items.summary: Visit LoveYourLiver.com and use code Dave2026 to access the special offer from de-liver-ance mentioned in this episode. Fatty Liver, GLP-1s, Alcohol, Hormones, Brain Fog, Weight Gain & Longevity Host Dave Asprey sits down with Siggi Clavien, Founder and CEO of The Liver Clinic and de-liver-ance, to explore why the liver may be one of the most overlooked organs in metabolism, hormone health, detoxification, brain function, weight management, and longevity. Siggi explains why fatty liver can develop without obvious symptoms and why someone can appear lean and healthy while still have significant liver fat. Drawing on thousands of liver scans, he shares what his team has observed in people whose blood markers appeared normal despite signs of fatty liver on imaging, and explains how tools such as FibroScan can reveal liver fat, stiffness, and fibrosis. Dave and Siggi go deep into triglycerides, cholesterol, insulin resistance, brain fog, weight gain, bile production, thyroid hormone activation, testosterone, estrogen metabolism, and liver regeneration. They also explore how alcohol, environmental chemicals, plastics, processed foods, artificial sweeteners, medications, and other exposures may place additional stress on the liver. items.title: They Lab Tested Retatrutide — The Results Were Shocking
items.summary: Are you actually getting the peptide you paid for? In this Peptide A to Z investigation, we look at independent laboratory testing of peptide products labeled Retatrutide and NAD+ that were purchased over the counter from a Brooklyn smoke shop. Four sealed vials were tested. Two were labeled Retatrutide 10mg. Two were labeled NAD+ 500mg. 🧬 FREE PEPTIDE GUIDE: Get the Peptide A to Z Guide and learn the basics of peptides, research, terminology, and more: PeptideAtoZ.com 👥 JOIN THE PEPTIDE A TO Z COMMUNITY: Connect with others interested in peptide research, longevity, and the latest peptide science: PeptideAtoZ.com According to the reported laboratory results, none of the four samples could be positively identified as the substance stated on the label. The retatrutide samples also produced an unexpected signal that the laboratory described as suggesting “extreme contamination.” But the story gets even more concerning. CBS News separately investigated a certificate of analysis associated with the retatrutide product. The laboratory named on that certificate reportedly told CBS that it never issued the certificate and had never had the company as a client. items.title: Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
items.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. My whole life doctors told me I'd need open heart surgery in my…

items.title: Top 3 Things To Improve Your Health
items.summary: Ep. 1,010: Join us as we sit down with Dr. William Li – an internationally renowned physician, scientist, and New York Times bestselling Author. His groundbreaking research has led to the development of more than 40 new medical treatments that impact care for more than 70 diseases including diabetes, blindness, heart disease and obesity. In this episode, Dr. William Li breaks down what actually happens inside the body when it comes to aging, disease, and cancer – and how much power we have through the choices we make every day. We dive into the foods that can support your body’s natural defenses, the everyday exposures that may be working against you, and the simple habits that can have a major impact on your health. Dr. Li also shares his approach to eating for longevity without fear or restriction, why gut health is so central to overall health, and the surprising role everyday beverages and pantry staples can play in your routine.

Catharine Arnston on Spirulina, Chlorella, Mitochondria, Detox, Brain Energy, and Longevity Could one of the oldest foods on Earth also be one of the most overlooked tools for mitochondrial health, brain function, detoxification, and longevity? Host Dave Asprey sits down with Catharine Arnston, founder of ENERGYbits and author of Love Your Health to Bits with Algae, to explore the biology of spirulina and chlorella and why these microscopic organisms have been studied for decades as unusually nutrient-dense foods. Catharine explains the major differences between spirulina and chlorella, from how they are grown and processed to how she uses them for completely different purposes. Spirulina contains compounds including phycocyanin and superoxide dismutase that Catharine believes can support mitochondrial function, antioxidant defenses, cellular energy, and brain health, while chlorella is used primarily for binding and removing unwanted compounds such as heavy metals. items.title: GLP-1s Are Melting Fat — But What About Your MUSCLE?
items.summary: GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound can produce dramatic weight loss. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? In this video, Peptide A to Z examines the growing concern around GLP-1 drugs and muscle loss. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. But the full story is more complicated than headlines suggesting these drugs simply “eat your muscle.” We break down: 💉 GLP-1 weight loss and lean mass 🔥 Fat loss vs. muscle loss 📊 What the STEP 1 semaglutide data actually showed 🫀 Why visceral fat matters 💪 Why preserving muscle becomes increasingly important with age 🧬 The new PROACT clinical trial 🔬 S-pindolol benzoate, also known as ACM-001.1 🏋️ Protein, resistance training and muscle preservation ⚖️ Why researchers are focusing on the quality of weight loss In the STEP 1 body-composition analysis, semaglutide was associated with approximately 19% lower total fat mass and 27% lower visceral fat, while lean body mass declined by about 10%. So yes, lean mass can decrease. But substantially more fat was lost, meaning overall body composition improved. Now researchers want to know whether they can do even better. The PROACT Phase 2 trial is studying whether an experimental drug called S-pindolol benzoate can help preserve lean body mass during semaglutide treatment. Researchers are also…

items.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
items.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. items.excerpt: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor.
